messages:
alana: Quick RFC follow-up: propose adding precision safepoints (two per transformer layer) and a transient dispatch context evaluated at each safepoint.
mike: Layer boundaries only? sounds safest to avoid KV cache churn.
jess: Agreed. post-layernorm->pre-attn and post-attn->pre-ffn are good spots.
zach: How to avoid kernel combinatorics? we currently key by op+dtype+hw.
alana: Use small per-op hints and build a dispatch table mapping (op, hint) -> ordered kernels. Runtime picks policy at safepoint and ops consult the transient context.
mike: That keeps metadata low. how do we override for canaries?
alana: Endpoint precision_policy merges at first safepoint; per-request headers allowed as opt-in token applied at safepoint.
nisha: Telemetry needs: safepoint policy id, chosen kernel tags, fallback events, and quant-table-version. sample payloads when fallback occurs.
zach: For sharded models prefer deterministic policy generation from stable inputs (model id, endpoint policy, request seed) so each device computes same context.
jess: And if a kernel fails at runtime, runtime should atomically switch to next candidate, emit fallback telemetry, and optionally snapshot minimal debug data.
ops-bot: Alert rule suggestion: create incident if fallback-rate > 0.5% over 5m; page if >2%.
alana: Proposed short plan: IR safepoint markers + runtime hook (1.5w), dispatch table + policy merge (2w), telemetry + QA harness (1.5w). feature-flag fast path (--force-dispatch) for early validation.
mike: Who owns what?
alana: I'll take IR/runtime hook. jess+zach take dispatch table and deterministic generator. nisha will spec telemetry & QA. mike maps SDK presets.
jess: I'll post a compact dispatch-table sketch tonight.
zach: I'll prototype the deterministic policy generator on shards.
alana: Thanks everyone. reconvene after initial PRs. :thumbsup:
